content.title: How Harry Kane's winning goal saw Bayern Munich edge past Real Madrid in the Champions League quarter-final
content.text: Bayern Munich left Madrid with a 2-1 first-leg advantage in their quarter-finalHarry Kane celebrates scoring for Bayern Munich against Real Madrid. Getty ImagesSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAnd what next for Real Madrid?The football never stops for Europe’s top teams and that much is true for Real Madrid who are in action again on Friday. They will host Girona at the Bernabeu in La Liga before heading to Munich for the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final next Wednesday.What next for Bayern Munich?Vincent Kompany’s side return to Bundesliga action on Saturday with a trip to St Pauli in Hamburg. Then they prepare for the big one and the arrival of Real Madrid at the Allianz Arena in the second leg of this tie next Wednesday.Real Madrid 1 Bayern Munich 2 – The BriefingWill anyone stop Harry Kane and Co?How did Upamecano miss that chance?Luis Diaz's trademark attacking rewardWhat will Thomas Tuchel have made of Alexander-Arnold?Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer remains eliteAnd where does this leave Real Madrid?Below, Dermot Corrigan, Sebastian Stafford-Bloor and Mark Carey dissect the key talking points at the Bernabeu.Enjoy.A wonderful display from Michael Olise A real joy to watch Michael Olise tonight. He was bold and brilliant with the ball at his feet, time and again getting the better of Alvaro Carreras. A goal would have capped off a special night for the winger, but an overhit pass from Luis Diaz late on robbed him of a great scoring chance. Let's hear from Vincent Kompany Getty ImagesThe Bayern Munich boss has been speaking to TNT Sports — this is how he reflected on that match:💬 “We are happy with what we have got. When the game comes to the Allianz, the same experience you felt in the last 15 minutes — you have to be up for the battle — you will feel at the Allianz. “I see no reason not to go into that game with more belief. The team has earned the right to be themselves, I don’t want to take away the chance to be themselves. “I don’t want to mix everything up. I haven’t thought too much about what has happened in the past (in the Champions League). The most important thing is to continue momentum. “I have a lot of respect for the opponent but a lot of confidence as well. I have hope we can go after a good result but you never know, it’s football.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNeuer: A goalkeeper who makes it look easy Getty ImagesHow manny clubs would like to have Manuel Neuer in their ranks? The answer I would guess is a lot — Bayern Munich can feel pleased to have had him at the top of his game for so long and tonight was no different. Here’s how Vincent Kompany reflected on his goalkeeper’s performance:💬 “He makes it look so easy, that’s what happens when you have great goalkeepers. They have a technique to get the ball away from teh danger area. The guys know that we will not go to the end of this competition if we do not have these types of performances.”Neuer superb for Bayern A word of appreciation for Bayern Munich's veteran goalkeeper Manuel Neuer. He may have recently turned 40 but Neuer was as sharp as he's ever been tonight, denying Vinicius Jr and Mbappe with several very strong saves. And he almost produced a remarkable stop to keep Mbappe out for Madrid's goal, but the Frenchman's shot just snuck through his glove. Photo of the night? Getty ImagesYou cannot beat a reverse angle of a goal and this one is a pretty good one, showing Harry Kane’s goal gliding past Lunin in the Madrid net.Bayern celebrate with their fans Getty ImagesThis is a big win for Bayern who have previously not had the best record at the Bernabeu.They celebrated with their fans at full time — Harry Kane looking on pretty pensively here.He explained to the media afterwards that nothing was wrong, he was just looking for his family in the crowd!Mbappe closing in on Ronaldo record As George referenced, Kylian Mbappe is closing in on Cristiano Ronaldo's record for the most goals in a season in the European Cup/Champions League.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMbappe adds to impressive tally Kylian Mbappe's goal tonight took his tally in the Champions League this season to 14. Only Cristiano Ronaldo (17, 16 and 15), Robert Lewandowski and Karim Benzema (both 15) have scored more in a single campaign. Bayern looking good for the titleWhat an enjoyable open game. I still think Bayern will win the whole thing.More from Arbeloa: ‘We can win anywhere’And here's more from Arbeloa, speaking to TNT Sports about goalscorer Mbappe:💬 “We know that Kylian had a great game. He scored one goal, he was a threat and for me he's the best player in the world.”On the return leg in Munich:“It's not going to be easy. I played there many times and we know the atmosphere always in the Allianz is not easy for opponents. “But we are Real Madrid — we can win anywhere.”Real Madrid are still alive in the tie.Over to Alvaro Arbeloa Getty ImagesHere's what the Madrid manager had to say to TNT Sports after his side's 2-1 defeat.He started by acknowledging the excellence of Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer: 💬 “He was MVP. We had so many chances to score more goals, we couldn't do it but we are still alive. We will go there with hope that we can win in Germany.“We lose two balls and they score two goals. We can't lose these types of balls because they are so fast, so quick, they have players with quality. “We can't make these types of mistakes.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementKane in the Champions League: 51 and counting... Harry Kane has now scored 51 goals in the Champions League — the same number as Thierry Henry.It also puts him three behind Mohamed Salah and six behind Erling Haaland and Thomas Muller. More from Harry KaneAnd here's more from goalscorer Harry Kane in his post-match interview with TNT Sports:💬 “We knew before the game all the hype around it. Coming to Madrid and the Bernabeu and trying to get a result is always a difficult thing to do. “We played some really good stuff today, for sure some areas we could have done better as well, maybe the final ball and the final finish, we had some good chances there. “But credit to them, they did as well and Manuel (Neuer) made some really good saves. Overall, we can be really happy with the win.”Kane: ‘We always feel dangerous’ Getty ImagesHarry Kane has been speaking to TNT Sports after today's game. Here's what he said:💬 “We've enjoyed some really good moments together. Obviously, we're in the business end of the season now so hopefully we can maintain that. “I think the more you play together, the more you train, the feelings get even stronger. “We always feel dangerous, we always feel like we can score goals for sure, and we did again away from home tonight.” Over to Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane...
